name: Spacecraft Systems: Solquint
subtitle: Spacecraft Systems Engineering
shortDescription: Size a satellite by building one: power, thermal, pointing, link and delta-v budgets, 13 cited labs and adaptive quizzes. Free core course.
longDescription:
Spacecraft Systems: Solquint teaches how a whole satellite fits together, one budget at a time. Every lesson is a piece of a spacecraft you could actually size: the solar array that must survive eclipse, the radiator that keeps the electronics warm, the wheels that point the camera, the antenna that closes the link.

Choose how to learn. The classical view walks 12 units and 80 topics in course order, from the space environment and the systems engineering process through power, thermal, attitude control, propulsion, structures, communications, onboard computing and ground operations to verification, cost and end of life. The real-world view hands you a mission instead, such as a 3U CubeSat, a 500 kg Earth observer or a constellation of eight 6U satellites, and opens the right lesson at the step where the numbers stop working. 14 build projects share one progress record with the course, so you can switch views at any time and keep everything.

Thirteen interactive labs run on your phone's graphics chip: orbit and eclipse shadow in 3D, solar array size against beta angle, a two-node thermal network, a link budget, Doppler over a ground pass, reaction wheel momentum, a B-dot detumble, a delta-v and mass optimiser, battery depth of discharge, orbit lifetime against drag, a pointing budget compared by root-sum-square and Monte Carlo, radiator sizing, and an illustrative shielding model. Each lab shows its formula, a cited source and an independent second route to the same answer.

Practice adapts to you. 720 original questions come on four levels from Beginner to Research. 480 are calculations whose answers were computed by two routes before being written in; 240 are concept items for practice only. The app tracks what you know, resurfaces what you are forgetting and sends you to the lesson behind each miss, in an encouraging voice. Choose 5, 10, 20 or 40 questions, or a length of your own. Twelve scenario case studies and two timed paper-style mocks finish the set.

Honest coverage: 41 of 80 topics map to a matching heading in an opened source (MIT OCW 16.851, NASA SmallSat State-of-the-Art, NASA Systems Engineering Handbook); 39 map more loosely and are marked so on the Coverage screen. Out of scope: optics, formation flight and reentry.

Sources open in a wide sheet with Back and Close. Text size runs from 50 to 300 percent. No sign-in, works offline and keeps your progress on the device.

Free: 7 of the 13 labs (eclipse and power, array against beta, link budget, thermal network, reaction wheel saturation, delta-v and mass, radiator sizing), 8 of the 14 builds, mock paper A, 6 of the 12 scenarios and levels 1 and 2. One optional monthly subscription, Solquint Plus Monthly, adds the other 6 labs (B-dot detumble, orbit lifetime, pointing budget, radiation dose, battery depth of discharge, Doppler pass), the other 6 builds, mock paper B, the other 6 scenarios and levels 3 and 4. Lessons, worked solutions and progress are never locked. The price is a single monthly amount that the store shows before you confirm. The plan auto-renews every month until cancelled, which you can do whenever you like in App Store or Google Play subscription settings. Cancelling ends the plan at the close of the month already paid: you keep Plus until then, pay for that month only and get no pro-rated partial-month charge. Refunds are requested from Apple or Google. Restore purchases is under More.

Study material only. Models are simplified; do not use it for flight hardware decisions. Not affiliated with any space agency, university or publisher named in the sources.
